## Workspace layout

`{baler}` is a CLI tool built in Rust and it is used to make `{box}` modules to be more manageable. What does the `crates/` workspace looks like?

```
crates/
├── baler-cli/              # bin + lib crate: clap CLI, thin command wrappers
│   └── src/
│       ├── lib.rs                 # Cli struct, clap subcommands, run()
│       ├── bin/baler.rs           # fn main() { baler_cli::run(); }
│       └── commands/              # one file per subcommand, delegates to baler-core::ops
├── baler-core/             # lib crate: all real logic, reusable outside the CLI
│   └── src/
│       ├── baler_toml/            # baler.toml schema + parsing, one file per table
│       ├── lockfile.rs            # baler.lock schema, read/write
│       ├── version.rs             # semver-based version requirements (module versions)
│       ├── ver.rs                 # R-native package versions and requirements
│       ├── resolver.rs            # PubGrub-based dependency solver
│       ├── paths.rs               # install-dir / R-lib-dir resolution
│       ├── formats/               # tar.gz archive read/write
│       ├── cran/                  # R package fetch, resolve, install
│       │   ├── packages.rs        # PACKAGES.gz fetch + parse
│       │   ├── universe.rs        # the CRAN side of the solver: repositories and Archive/ lookups
│       │   ├── client.rs          # dependency resolution + install orchestration
│       │   ├── client/            # graph.rs (resolution), download.rs (source installs), git.rs (GitHub packages)
│       │   └── binary_install.rs  # binary-archive extraction
│       └── ops/                   # one module per CLI command's actual logic
│           ├── init.rs, bundle.rs, compile.rs, lock.rs, remove.rs
│           ├── resolve.rs, module_graph.rs, external_tools.rs
│           └── install.rs         # with install/: archive.rs, github.rs, native.rs
└── native-code-handler/    # the `baler-native` package: compiled-code scaffolding and build
    └── src/
        ├── detect.rs      # locates native-code dirs inside a module's source tree
        ├── scaffold.rs    # writes example native code for `baler init --native`
        ├── toolchain.rs   # R CMD SHLIB invocation, target/arch detection, .abi.json sidecars
        ├── cache.rs       # build cache, keyed by source hash, platform, and R version
        ├── lang.rs        # NativeLang / Backend enums
        └── templates/     # per-language scaffold templates (c, cpp, fortran, R glue)
```

`baler-cli` owns argument parsing and process exit codes. `baler-core` owns everything that could plausibly be reused by something other than the CLI, and the `network` feature flag lives on this crate. `baler-native` (the package in the `native-code-handler/` directory) owns everything to do with locating, scaffolding, and building a module's compiled code, independent of both the CLI and the packaging logic in `baler-core`.

## What goes into a bundle

`baler bundle` writes a `<name>_<version>.tar.gz` that contains a single top-level directory, `<name>_<version>/`:

```
tstk_0.1.0/
├── tstk/              # the module's source directory (the one with __init__.r)
│   ├── __init__.r
│   └── ...
├── baler.toml
└── baler.lock         # only if the project has one
```

`baler.toml` and `baler.lock` are shipped as they are, not as a generated copy of them, much like a Python sdist ships its own `pyproject.toml`. `baler install` reads `baler.toml` back out of the archive, so the archive is self-describing without a second metadata file. Earlier versions embedded a generated `manifest.json` here, but it duplicated `baler.toml` and has been removed.

Which files are included:

- Every file under the module's source directory, except hidden (dot-prefixed) files and directories, which are never bundled.
- The one exception is `.lib/`, which is dot-prefixed but is forced into the archive when `binary = true` is set under `[compiled-code]`. Binaries are stored per platform as `.lib/<platform>/`, each artifact with an `.abi.json` sidecar. See [Binary bundles](../reference/native-code.qmd#binary-bundles) for what install does with them.
- The native source, always. `binary` only decides whether compiled binaries ship along with it.

## Path resolution

Two directories matter at runtime, and both follow an environment-variable-first, sensible-default-second pattern.

::: panel-tabset

### Module install directory

Under `paths::resolve_install_dir()`:

1. `BALER_LIB`, if set and non-empty.
2. `~/.baler/modules`.

### R user library directory

Under `paths::resolve_r_lib_dir()`:

1. `BALER_R_LIB`, if set and non-empty. The explicit override, meant for renv/rv-style project-local libraries.
2. `R_LIBS_USER`, if set and non-empty. R's own variable.
3. A subprocess fallback: `Rscript -e "cat(.libPaths()[1])"`.

The third step is a real subprocess call. Invoking `baler install --install-deps` without `R`/`Rscript` on `PATH`, and without either environment variable set, fails there with an error asking whether R is installed and on `PATH`. If `Rscript` runs but reports no library path, the error points at `BALER_R_LIB` instead.

:::

The build cache has its own override, `BALER_CACHE_DIR`, described under [Build cache](../reference/native-code.qmd#build-cache).
